rule.title: Dual-Token Architecture (15m Memory Access + 7d HttpOnly Cookie Refresh)
rule.statement: JWT access tokens must have a short lifespan (<= 15 minutes) kept in memory, while refresh tokens (7 days) must be stored in an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie.
rule.rationale: Storing long-lived tokens in localStorage exposes them to XSS theft. Storing refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies prevents client-side script access.
rule.implementation_guidance: Set cookie with { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'strict', path: '/api/v1/auth' } on login.

forbidden.example: Returning both access and refresh tokens in JSON to be saved in window.localStorage.

preferred.example: res.cookie('refreshToken', token, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'strict' });

source.book_title: Alice and Bob Learn Application Security
source.evidence_quote: Cookies containing session tokens must always have the httpOnly flag set to protect them from XSS theft, and the Secure flag to ensure transmission over HTTPS only.

rule.title: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for Sensitive Administrative Operations
rule.statement: Security-sensitive operations (password reset, email change, organization deletion, API key generation) must require step-up MFA verification.
rule.rationale: If a user's session token is compromised, step-up MFA prevents the attacker from permanently hijacking the account or deleting data.
rule.implementation_guidance: Verify TOTP code (otplib) or email OTP before committing credential mutations.

forbidden.example: Allowing password updates with only an active session and no re-authentication.

preferred.example: if (!totp.verify({ token, secret })) throw new AppError(401, 'INVALID_2FA', 'Invalid 2FA code');

source.book_title: Alice and Bob Learn Application Security
source.evidence_quote: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requires two or more distinct verification factors, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized account takeovers.
